25: }

27: // Old-style callback query. Accepts a table name and a predicate.
28: export function query(table, predicate, callback) {
29:   setImmediate(() => {
30:     const rows = tables[table];
31:     if (!rows) return callback(new Error(`no such table: ${table}`));
32:     try {
33:       callback(null, rows.filter(predicate).map((r) => ({ ...r })));
34:     } catch (err) {
35:       callback(err);
36:     }
37:   });
38: }
39: 
40: export function update(table, id, patch, callback) {
41:   setImmediate(() => {
42:     const row = (tables[table] || []).find((r) => r.id === id);
43:     if (!row) return callback(new Error(`no row ${id} in ${table}`));
44:     Object.assign(row, patch);
45:     callback(null, { ...row });
46:   });
47: }

part.text:
Ran `npm test` (`node --test`): **10 tests total — 7 passed, 3 failed.**

| Failing test | Expected vs. actual | Why it fails |
|---|---|---|
| `findByEmail ignores soft-deleted users` — `tests/auth-service.test.js:5` | Expected `null`; returned Alan’s user record with `deleted_at: '2026-01-04'`. | `src/services/auth-service.js:5` filters only by email, so soft-deleted users are included. |
| `totalPaidCents counts only paid orders` — `tests/order-service.test.js:14` | Expected **14,600** cents; received **1,350**. | `src/services/order-service.js:9` selects orders with `status === 'quote'`, so it sums the quote order instead of the paid orders. |
| `uncapturedTotalCents sums uncaptured payments` — `tests/payment-service.test.js:14` | Expected **9,900** cents; received **4,200**. | `src/services/payment-service.js:10` selects `captured === true`, so it sums captured payments instead of uncaptured ones. |

The nested assertion errors in the output occur because `src/db.js:32–35` catches assertions thrown inside the test callbacks and invokes those callbacks again with the assertion as an error.

No files were changed.
